rationale: Round-2 codebase-pin re-review of f490fd26. CLASSIFICATION OF MY TWO ROUND-1 ASKS: (1) structural cell cross-pin — ADDRESSED per my stated acceptance bar, with one NEW_ISSUE found re-deriving (below); (2) blocked-child leg — ADDRESSED. Ask 1 evidence, all probes run in fresh /tmp copies: my round-1 probe (complete->review's three doc cells to `plan`, doc only) now fails with a precise cells-differ diff; a single-cell probe (terminal row's Derivation `done`->`idle`, the subtlest drift) also fails; the parser reads all four cells and the comparison is bidirectional; rowFixtures makes a row identifier without an executable fixture a loud t.Fatalf. Ask 2 evidence: rowCompleteImplementMidSpec now fixtures closed+open+blocked (task b5-3 "blocked"), the guide's row-5 note says fixture-backed, and the suite is green. NEW_ISSUE (MAJOR, discovered probing my own ask's fix past its stated acceptance bar): the header's strongest claim — "editing the doc AND this slice to an incorrect value together still fails, because the fixture's assertion is checked against REAL production code... which cannot be made to agree with a wrong record" (agreement_table_test.go:22-27) — is empirically FALSE for the seven wireEpicFixture three-surface rows (spec approve through complete->review). I edited BOTH the doc row and the agreementTableRows entry for complete->review to plan/plan/plan, children left all-closed, and the suite stayed GREEN. Mechanism: those rows seed the fixture epic's stored phase FROM row.derivation (e.g. v2Epic(epicID, specID, "open", row.derivation, ...)), and DerivePhaseWithStatusWithCache is stored-authoritative (derive.go:176-179 — on disagreement it warns to stderr and returns storedPhase, "trusting stored phase"; the test reads no stderr), so the record's value round-trips through all three surfaces no matter what the children say. Consequence: rows 2-8 verify surface CONSISTENCY given a stored value but do not pin the shipped child derivation at all — a regression in DerivePhaseFromChildren's branches would leave them green (only the release/repair rows 9-12, which drive SanctionedDerivedSync / EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 / DerivePhaseFromChildren directly, genuinely pin code). R1.3's "cross-checked... against the shipped derivation, so the table cannot silently drift from code" is over-claimed for those rows, and this is the exact vacuous-anti-drift class that hard-blocked round 1 — now one layer deeper. The fix is small and contained to the test file. Everything else this round is solid: the two new repair-phase rows drive the real EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 (marker key and value asserted) and prove row 12's backward premise via IsBackwardMove against the real comparator; the force-reason key matches repair.go:300; the terminal-row tautology is gone (preconditions walked, stateShow checked against the one reachable literal); go build + internal/phase -short green from the bead worktree; worktree left clean and byte-identical (probe copies in /tmp restored). REQUEST_CHANGES, no hard block: the operator-facing drift vector (doc edits) is genuinely closed; the residual is a false documented claim plus a circular code-leg, fixable with one non-circular assertion per row.
concrete_changes_required: Break the stored-echo circularity for the seven wireEpicFixture three-surface rows: add a non-circular code leg asserting the row's child state genuinely derives its mode — e.g. in assertThreeSurfaces (or per-row), assert phase.DerivePhaseFromChildren(children) == row.derivation (passing the fixture's children through; for spec-approve's nil children the empty-set fallback correctly yields plan). Acceptance probe: editing BOTH the doc row and the agreementTableRows entry for `complete → review (last bead)` to plan/plan/plan (children unchanged, all closed) must turn the suite red — today it stays green.

Correct the file-header claim (agreement_table_test.go:19-27) to match whatever the fixed mechanism actually guarantees; as shipped, the "cannot be made to agree with a wrong record" sentence is demonstrably false for rows whose fixtures seed stored phase from row.derivation.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE: three-way pin is circular for the seven stored-seeded rows — coordinated doc+record falsification stays green
findings.detail: Empirically demonstrated in a /tmp copy of f490fd26: sed both project-docs/user/guides/lifecycle-modes.md's `complete → review (last bead)` cells AND its agreementTableRows entry to plan/plan/plan (fixture children still b8-1/b8-2 closed) — `go test -short -run TestAgreementTable ./internal/phase/` passes. Cause: rowCompleteReviewLastBead (and rows spec-approve, plan-approve, next-claim, complete-implement, both complete-plan rows) construct the epic with storedPhase = row.derivation, and DerivePhaseWithStatusWithCache returns the stored value on disagreement (derive.go:176-179, "trusting stored phase" — stderr warning only, unread by the test); ResolveModeWithCache and the tail context read the same stored-authoritative value. So the record feeds itself back through every surface. The header comment at agreement_table_test.go:22-27 claims this exact attack fails; it does not. These rows therefore do not pin the shipped child derivation (rows 9-12 do, via SanctionedDerivedSync / EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 / DerivePhaseFromChildren), leaving R1.3's "cannot silently drift from code" only true for doc-only edits.
